5852a6bc3cac355c497c3c1e51f8e329670dca6f.summary: Securonix Threat Research describes the STARK#MULE campaign, which sends phishing zip attachments with US military recruitment-themed lures aimed at Korean-speaking victims. The malware is staged from two compromised Korean e-commerce websites. It runs PowerShell, sets up daily scheduled tasks for persistence, and communicates over HTTP. The report says the actor possibly originates from North Korea, pending confirmation, and compares the activity to the APT37 group.
